newsitem.title: UK: NWE straight-run fuel oil offers rise on crude.
newsitem.headline: NWE straight-run fuel oil offers rise on crude.

text.p: European low sulphur straight-run ended a quiet week on Friday talked firmer but with buyers still far from sellers, some of whom uped their price on positive sentiment from crude's gains.

One of the only two sellers with 0.5 to 0.7 percent material increased his asking price $1 to $100/$101 a tonne while the second was steady at $98. Bids were in the $96/$98 area but no deals were reported done.
The first seller said it saw a bid at $98 per tonne but rejected it "because I think it (low-sulphur straight run) will improve."
The seller added: "We're not in a hurry to sell and we're hoping to achieve three figures...With crude improving you would expect us to improve from yesterday's range."
Traders said some buying interest was coming in from the United States.
"The only problem is with the high freight rates which have to be factored into the bids, especially to the United States...This makes it difficult to reach a right price," one trader said.
